title: Derived sections of one root-tower term with profinite parameters
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a norm-topological finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ containing $E$ with the extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ put $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ for every profinite set $P$, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], ordinary unbounded derived categories and total derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $V\to Y$ be an affine etale chart on which the only boundary components present are $V(t_1),\ldots,V(t_r)$, for a reduced strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]; set $Z=V(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ and $V^\circ=V[1/(t_1\cdots t_r)]$. For $r=0$ take $Z=V^\circ=V$. For an affine pro-etale $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to V$, put $S=U\times_V Z$ and
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_1^{1/n},\ldots,x_r^{1/n}]/((x_i^{1/n})^n-t_i)_{i=1}^r\right),\qquad T^\circ=T\times_VV^\circ.$$
The index is ordered by divisibility and the transition sends $x_i^{1/n}$ to $(x_i^{1/m})^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$. Write $j:T^\circ\hookrightarrow T$, $v:T^\circ\to U$, and $s:S\hookrightarrow U$. Setting every root to zero gives $i:S\to T$. When $r=0$ the tower is $T=T^\circ=U$ and $i=s=\mathrm{id}_U$.
For $F=E$ or $\Omega$ let $\mathcal N$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{F,T}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], and fix $i^*\mathcal N\cong p_S^*M_F$, where $M$ is a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space, $M_F(P)=C(P,F\otimes_E M)$, and $F\otimes_E M$ has its finite-dimensional product norm topology. For every profinite set $P$ form $T^\circ[P]$ as in [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], let $v_P:T^\circ[P]\to U$ be the composite, and pull $j^*\mathcal N$ to $T^\circ[P]$. Let $C_F[P]$ be the free internal $C_F$-module on the condensed set $Q\mapsto C(Q,P)$, and write $R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}$ for the right derived internal module Hom. Then restriction of sections and derived adjunction give a natural isomorphism
$$s^*R(v_P)_*(\mathcal N|_{T^\circ[P]}[0])\ \cong\ p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F).$$
It is natural in $P$, in morphisms of the supplied extensions $\mathcal N$, and under pro-etale base change of $U$. It respects automorphisms of the root tower, including continuous profinite families of such automorphisms together with their equivariant actions on $\mathcal N$. For a family indexed by $Q$, the compatibility is the equality of morphisms on the $Q$-parametrized terms, not merely equality after evaluation at each point of $Q$. On degree zero its map is restriction to $S$ of the sections on the full root tower; for $P=*$ it is the inverse of the map induced by $\mathcal N\to Rj_*j^*\mathcal N$. The comparison maps are compatible for $E\to\Omega$ whenever the supplied extensions and boundary identifications are obtained from one $E$-extension by ordinary scalar extension. This compatibility is after scalar restriction and uses the actual map $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Only one term of the root-cover nerve is being computed; no derived invariants or total nerve is identified here. Free internal module means the left adjoint to forgetting a module to a condensed set. Internal module Hom is the right adjoint of internal module tensor; its right derived functor is computed by injective resolutions in its second variable. These are taken in coefficient universes containing the small site and the profinite parameter sets.

proof.text:
Write $q:T\to U$, $\pi_P:T[P]\to T$, and $\mathcal N_P=\pi_P^*\mathcal N$. Pulling a finite-free trivialization back shows $\mathcal N_P$ is lisse; the root equations commute with $U[P]\to U$. Apply puncture invariance with all coordinates: the actual unit $\mathcal N_P[0]\to Rj_{P,*}j_P^*\mathcal N_P[0]$ is invertible. Normalized derived composition identifies its image under $s^*Rq_{P,*}$ with
$$\lambda_P:s^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}s^*Rv_{P,*}j_P^*\mathcal N_P[0].$$

The parameter-root geometry lemma gives integral $q_P$ and the surjective closed $a_P:S[P]\to T[P]\times_U S$, with $h_Pa_P=i_P$ and $q_{S,P}a_P=\rho_P$. Thus the fibre-section specialization applies with $X=T$, $Z=S$, $\mathcal L=\mathcal N$, giving the normalized restriction isomorphism
$$\theta_P:s^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\rho_{P,*}(\rho_P^*i^*\mathcal N[0]).$$
This uses the nil-fibre unit, not equality of the two fibre schemes.

Pull back $i^*\mathcal N\cong p_S^*M_F$ along $\rho_P$, using point-pullback composition. Since $S$ is closed in affine $U$, it is affine. The profinite-functions comparison with $X=S$ and the supplied finite-dimensional $M$ composes with $\theta_P$ to give $\gamma_P$ from the full source to $p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F)$. Set $\alpha_P=\gamma_P\lambda_P^{-1}$. This is an isomorphism of derived objects.

The normalization of $\theta$ and of the function comparison makes $H^0(\gamma_P)$ restriction of full-tower sections followed by evaluation as functions. At $P=*$ evaluation is the identity, so under $\theta_*$ the map $\alpha_*$ is the inverse of the open unit. Naturality of the puncture unit, specialization and functions gives the required squares for $\alpha$. Apply these squares on $U[Q]$, with the supplied module action and parameter maps, to get equality over the whole $Q$-test scheme. For scalars the specialization cospan and function comparison use the actual $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ after restriction; naturality of the open unit gives its cospan too. Cancelling the invertible $\lambda_E,\lambda_\Omega$ gives the stated compatibility without inverting a directional scalar-restriction map.

For $r=0$, $T=T^\circ=U=S$ and $\lambda_P=1$, so this is exactly the parameter-functions comparison. For $P=\varnothing$ both the free module and the direct image from the empty test scheme are zero. Rank zero or empty $S$ gives zero on both sides. Finite $P$ gives the finite product of the one-point models; no cohomology/limit interchange is used.
